Multiple-decrement CoDa model of causes of death (experimental)

Source: R/model-coda.R
coda_causes.Rd

coda_causes() forecasts death rates by cause with the multiple-decrement form of the compositional Lee-Carter model, which Oeppen (2008) proposed and tested on Japanese causes of death. Causes add up to all causes in every draw. The model is experimental.

Usage

coda_causes(
  var = "cause",
  total_level = "all",
  jump_off = c("observed", "fitted"),
  residual = "auto"
)

Arguments

var

Stratum variable with the causes.

total_level

Level of var for all causes.

jump_off

"observed" (forecasts start from the observed deaths of the last year) or "fitted" (from the fitted deaths).

residual

Add a residual cause, the part of all-cause mortality not covered by the listed causes: TRUE, FALSE, or "auto" (added when the listed causes leave more than 0.1% of all-cause mortality unexplained in the median cell).

Value

A model specification.

Details

Only the abstract of Oeppen (2008) is published. This function implements the natural multiple-decrement form of coda():

  1. in each group (the strata that differ only in var, for example one group per sex), the cause-specific rates m[x, c] add up to all-cause rates m[x], which give life-table deaths d[x] with radix 1 (life_table() conventions); the deaths are split by cause, d[x, c] = d[x] m[x, c] / m[x] (multiple-decrement life table);

  2. the composition is the joint distribution of the deaths d[x, c] over age and cause, plus the survivors at the upper bound of a closed age range;

  3. as in coda(), the composition is centred by its closed geometric mean over the years and transformed by the centred log-ratio; the first component of a singular value decomposition gives b[x, c] k[t], and k[t] follows a random walk with drift;

  4. forecast deaths d[x, c] give all-cause rates from the all-cause life-table deaths d[x] = sum_c d[x, c], and cause-specific rates m[x, c] = m[x] d[x, c] / d[x].

The causes add up to the all-cause rates in every draw, and the strata of total_level get their sum. If the listed causes leave part of the all-cause deaths unexplained (residual), that part is a residual cause inside the model and counts towards the all-cause rates; it is not a stratum of the output.

One index k[t] drives all ages and causes, so the causes cannot follow different trends beyond the pattern b[x, c]. The extensions of Kjærgaard, Ergemen, Kallestrup-Lamb, Oeppen and Lindahl-Jacobsen (2019) are not implemented. In a backtest on mt_example_causes() the model was less accurate than cause_shares(); compare it with cause_shares() or reconciled() separate models in a backtest before using it.

Jump-off, the open age interval and zero deaths are treated as in coda(): the all-cause log rate of an open interval is regressed on k[t] (its split by cause comes from the composition), and zero rates of a cause are replaced by half its smallest positive rate in the group (as replace.zeros() of the R package MortalityForecast). Draws are expected rates. Predictive draws (mt_forecast(predictive = TRUE)) add extra-Poisson and Poisson variation to the all-cause rates and split the all-cause deaths multinomially between the causes, so that the causes also add up to all causes in predictive draws.

References

Oeppen J (2008). Coherent forecasting of multiple-decrement life tables: a test using Japanese cause of death data. CODAWORK'08, Universitat de Girona.

Bergeron-Boucher M-P, Canudas-Romo V, Oeppen J, Vaupel JW (2017). Coherent forecasts of mortality with compositional data analysis. Demographic Research 37(17): 527-566. doi:10.4054/DemRes.2017.37.17

Kjærgaard S, Ergemen YE, Kallestrup-Lamb M, Oeppen J, Lindahl-Jacobsen R (2019). Forecasting causes of death by using compositional data analysis: the case of cancer deaths. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series C 68(5): 1351-1370. doi:10.1111/rssc.12357

See also

cause_shares(), coda().

Examples

x <- mt_example_causes(years = 2005:2019)
fit <- mt_fit(coda_causes(), x)
fc <- mt_forecast(fit, h = 5, n_draws = 50, seed = 1)
